project_title: The Gut Microbiome Composition Associates with Bipolar Disorder and Illness Severity
project_description: Case-control study using 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V4 region) of stool samples from 115 individuals with bipolar disorder and 64 healthy controls from the Prechter Longitudinal Study of Bipolar Disorder (University of Michigan).
citation: Evans et al. 2017, J Psychiatr Res, PMID 27988330
notes: Fractional representation significantly decreased (34% lower) in bipolar disorder vs controls after adjustment for age, sex, BMI and FDR correction; abstract states p<0.001. Within BD patients, lower Faecalibacterium also associated with worse self-reported physical/mental health, sleep quality, anxiety and mania scores.

project_title: Perturbations in Gut Microbiota Composition in Psychiatric Disorders: A Review and Meta-analysis
project_description: Umbrella systematic review and meta-analysis of 59 case-control gut microbiota studies across adult psychiatric disorders (16S rRNA/shotgun metagenomics), including 9 case-control comparisons totaling 465 patients with bipolar disorder.
citation: Nikolova et al. 2021, JAMA Psychiatry, PMID 34524405
notes: Depleted Faecalibacterium was one of the most consistent transdiagnostic findings, reported as decreased across major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, psychosis/schizophrenia, and anxiety (a marker of reduced anti-inflammatory butyrate-producing bacteria); no BD-specific exact p-value given in extractable abstract text.
